notes: This contract pins the complete official C++ BasicDataElements helper catalog as a bounded SDK foundation. The selected IEEE 1516.1-2025 C++ requirement requires encoding helpers to encode and decode standard HLA byte arrays. Umbra implements the Table 29 IEEE 1516.2-2025 HLAinteger16BE, HLAinteger16LE, HLAunsignedInteger16BE, HLAunsignedInteger16LE, HLAoctetPairBE, HLAoctetPairLE, HLAinteger32LE, HLAunsignedInteger32LE, HLAinteger64BE, HLAinteger64LE, HLAunsignedInteger64BE, HLAunsignedInteger64LE, HLAfloat32BE/LE, HLAfloat64BE/LE, and HLAoctet representations, plus the Table 32 HLAbyte, HLAASCIIchar, and HLAunicodeChar mappings and the Table 35 HLAASCIIstring/HLAunicodeString mappings. The 16-bit helpers use their prescribed two-octet widths, endian order, signed two's-complement interpretation where applicable, and octet boundary value two; the 32-bit little-endian helpers use their prescribed four-octet width, endian order, signed two's-complement interpretation where applicable; the 64-bit helpers use their prescribed eight-octet widths, endian order, signed two's-complement interpretation where applicable; the float helpers use bit-preserving IEEE 754 conversion and explicitly require 32-bit/64-bit IEC 559 native float/double support; raw octet/byte values preserve their single octet; the ASCII helpers reject non-ASCII octets; HLAunicodeChar represents exactly one UTF-16BE code unit; and HLAunicodeString rejects unmatched UTF-16 surrogates in both encoding directions. HLAASCIIstring and HLAunicodeString use the separately traced HLAvariableArray signed HLAinteger32BE element count. The exact Table 29/Table 32/Table 35/Table 43 cells are source-checked but are not individually exported as immutable helper requirement candidates; RL-053 records that Requirements Lab boundary. This does not establish generic constructed-data encoding, package/JUnit/protected-review evidence, interoperability, or conformance.
